title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. C2-C8 are out of scope for this plan because they require 12 datasets and would take hours; the code is dataset-agnostic if extended.

"""Dataset loading for the proximity-kernel reproduction (Table 2/3 datasets).

Only the target-claim dataset (Hepatitis) is needed for the main run; the loader is
written so that more UCI datasets can be added cheaply later.
"""
import io
import os
import urllib.request

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HEPATITIS_URL = (
    "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data"
)
# UCI files use '?' for missing; some mirrors use blanks / 'NaN'.
NA_VALUES = ["?", "", " ", "NaN", "nan", "NA", "None"]


def cache_dirs():
    dirs = []
    base = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if base:
        dirs.append(os.path.join(base, "files"))
        dirs.append(base)
    dirs.append(os.path.join(".cache"))
    return dirs


def fetch(url, filename):
    """Return a local path for `url`, checking the shared cache first."""
    for d in cache_dirs():
        p = os.path.join(d, filename)
        if os.path.isfile(p) and os.path.getsize(p) > 0:
            return p
    last_err = None
    for d in cache_dirs():
        try:
            os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError:
            continue
        dest = os.path.join(d, filename)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r:
                data = r.read()
            with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                f.write(data)
            return dest
        except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover - network dependent
            last_err = e
    raise RuntimeError(f"could not fetch {url}: {last_err}")


def load_hepatitis():
    """UCI Hepatitis: 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes (Table 2)."""
    path = fetch(HEPATITIS_URL, "hepatitis.data")
    df = pd.read_csv(path, header=None, na_values=NA_VALUES)
    assert df.shape == (155, 20), df.shape
    y_raw = df.iloc[:, 0].to_numpy()
    # UCI coding: 1 = die, 2 = live -> relabel to 0/1
    y = (y_raw.astype(int) - 1).astype(int)
    X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).to_numpy()
    meta = {
        "name": "Hepatitis",
        "uci_id": 46,
        "url": HEPATITIS_URL,
        "n_samples": int(X.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_classes": int(len(np.unique(y))),
        "class_counts": {int(k): int(v) for k, v in zip(*np.unique(y, return_counts=True))},
        "n_missing": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "missing_pct": float(100.0 * np.isnan(X).sum() / X.size),
        "missing_per_feature": {int(j): int(v) for j, v in enumerate(np.isnan(X).sum(0))},
    }
    return X, y, meta

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (Section 4 of the paper).

Pipeline (faithful to the paper):
  4.1.1 Eq. (4)  per-feature bin centers = evenly spaced percentiles of the OBSERVED
                 values: percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)), k=1..nbins.
                 (so c_{j,1}=min and c_{j,nbins}=max, as the paper states)
  4.1.2 Eq. (5)  proximity assignment: b_i,j = argmin_k |x_i,j - c_j,k|
  4.1.3 Eqs. (6)-(7) one-hot encoding for observed entries, concatenated over d features
  4.2   Eqs. (8)-(14) three-level cascading fallback for missing entries
  4.3   Eq. (15) K(x_m,x_n) = (1/d) z_m^T z_n
"""
import numpy as np


def fit_bins(X, nbins, method="linear"):
    """Eq. (4): bin centers as evenly spaced percentiles of the observed values."""
    n, d = X.shape
    centers = np.zeros((d, nbins), dtype=float)
    prior = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins, dtype=float)
    has_obs = np.zeros(d, dtype=bool)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            # A7: entirely missing feature -> uniform centers/prior
            centers[j] = np.arange(nbins, dtype=float)
            continue
        has_obs[j] = True
        if nbins == 1:
            centers[j] = np.array([np.median(obs)])
        else:
            qs = np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)
            centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, qs, method=method)
        # Eq. (13): global prior over bins for this feature
        counts = np.array([(assign_bins_1d(obs, centers[j]) == k).sum() for k in range(nbins)],
                          dtype=float)
        prior[j] = counts / counts.sum()
    return centers, prior, has_obs


def assign_bins_1d(values, centers):
    """Eq. (5) for a 1-d array of values; ties -> lowest bin index (np.argmin)."""
    return np.argmin(np.abs(values[:, None] - centers[None, :]), axis=1)


def assign_bins(X, centers):
    """Return integer bin assignments B (n,d); -1 for missing entries."""
    n, d = X.shape
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        col = X[:, j]
        obs = ~np.isnan(col)
        if obs.any():
            B[obs, j] = assign_bins_1d(col[obs], centers[j])
    return B

    """Eq. (6): binary one-hot vectors for observed entries (zeros for missing)."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    ii, jj = np.where(B >= 0)
    H[ii, jj, B[ii, jj]] = 1.0
    return H


def cascading_fallback(X, B, H_obs, prior, nbins, mode="restricted", stats=None):
    """Eqs. (8)-(14): fill encodings of missing entries.

    mode="restricted": kernel mean embedding averaged over matching samples m that
        have feature j OBSERVED (denominator = number of such samples).  Keeps
        h_i,j a probability distribution over bins (rows sum to 1).
    mode="literal": the paper's literal Eq. (10)/(12), denominator |S1(i)| / |S2(i)|,

        Rows then need not sum to 1.

def read_contract_target(claim_id="C1"):
    """Read the target value from the provided claim contract (never hard-coded)."""
    if not os.path.isfile(CONTRACT):
        return None
    try:
        with open(CONTRACT, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            contract = json.load(f)
        for c in contract.get("claims", []):
            if c.get("id") == claim_id:
                m = re.search(r"NMI\s+([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+)\s+on", c.get("statement", ""))
                if m:
                    return float(m.group(1))
    except Exception:
        return None
    return None


def baseline_median_imputation_nmi(X, y, n_clusters, seeds):
    """Sanity reference: median imputation + K-means (not part of the claim)."""
    Xi = SimpleImputer(strategy="median").fit_transform(X)
    nmis = [float(normalized_mutual_info_score(
        y, KMeans(n_clusters=n_clusters, n_init=N_INIT, random_state=s).fit_predict(Xi)))
        for s in seeds]
    return {"mean_nmi": float(np.mean(nmis)), "per_seed_nmi": nmis}


def bin_centers_variant(X, nbins, scheme):
    """Alternative bin-center schemes used only for the sensitivity analysis."""
    d = X.shape[1]
    centers = np.zeros((d, nbins))
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            centers[j] = np.arange(nbins, dtype=float)

        if scheme == "paper_eq4":            # 0..100 inclusive (Eq. 4)

        elif scheme == "quantile_edges":      # 100*k/nbins for k=1..nbins
            qs = 100.0 * np.arange(1, nbins + 1) / nbins
        elif scheme == "interior":            # 100*k/(nbins+1) for k=1..nbins
            qs = 100.0 * np.arange(1, nbins + 1) / (nbins + 1)
        else:
            raise ValueError(scheme)
        centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, qs, method="linear")
    return centers

    """Same pipeline as the paper but with externally supplied bin centers."""
    B = pk.assign_bins(X, centers)
    H_obs = pk.onehot_observed(B, nbins)

    for j in range(X.shape[1]):

        prior[j] = cnt / max(cnt.sum(), 1.0)
    H, _ = pk.cascading_fallback(X, B, H_obs, prior, nbins, mode=mode)
    return H.reshape(X.shape[0], X.shape[1] * nbins)

audit_summary: The reproducer implements the paper's full proximity-kernel pipeline (Eq. 4 percentile bin centers -> Eq. 5 nearest-center assignment -> Eqs. 6-7 one-hot encoding -> Eqs. 8-14 three-level cascading fallback -> Eq. 15 normalized inner product) on the real UCI Hepatitis file (155x19, 167/2945 = 5.67% missing, 2 classes, matching Table 2), clustered transductively with sklearn KMeans at K=2 and scored with sklearn NMI averaged over 10 seeds, with the nbins grid {2,3,4,6,8} searched and fully logged. The clean re-run reproduced NMI = 0.228909 (diff +0.0000 vs the contract target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02) in 25 s with exit 0; nothing is hard-coded (no paper constants appear in the code, and the contract value is only read to print the pass/fail check) and all reported numbers come from the computed representation (Z shape (155,38), kernel symmetry/max, fallback level counts, sensitivity variants). No scale-down occurred: full dataset, full 10 seeds, full hyperparameter grid, no subsetting or reduced epochs. Two caveats worth recording: the level-3 global-prior path is implemented but never triggered on Hepatitis (level3=0), and the exact percentile convention in Eq. 4 is underspecified (assumption A2) - alternative bin-center conventions in the workspace's own sensitivity table give markedly lower values (0.099-0.180 at nbins=2), so the match relies on the endpoint-inclusive percentile reading, though the 'literal' vs 'restricted' fallback variants (assumption A8) agree exactly at the selected nbins. Claims C2-C8 (other datasets, averages, HI-PMK baseline) were not reproduced - only the Hepatitis loader exists - so this audit only certifies the match target C1.

requirement_check.evidence: src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins() computes centers per feature from `obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]`, i.e. observed values only; missing entries are excluded from the percentile computation.

fit_bins uses qs = np.linspace(0, 100, nbins) with numpy linear-interpolation percentiles, so centers are evenly spaced percentiles of the observed distribution. Convention is underspecified (assumption A2); the workspace also reports two alternative schemes (quantile_edges, interior) in metrics.json/sensitivity, which give clearly lower NMI, so the exact percentile convention materially affects the value.
assign_bins_1d uses np.argmin(|x - c_k|) (Eq. 5) with lowest-index tie-break (assumption A3); B = -1 for missing entries.
onehot_observed builds binary h_{i,j} in {0,1}^nbins and build_representation concatenates to Z with shape (n, d*nbins) = (155, 38) at nbins=2.

cascading_fallback implements the per-missing-entry cascade intersection (S1) -> union (S2) -> global prior with a level counter; metrics.json records level counts observed=2778, level1=61, level2=106, level3=0 for the selected setting.

Level 1 in cascading_fallback averages H_obs over S1 members that observe feature j (assumption A8, 'restricted'); the literal denominator-|S1| variant ('literal' mode) is also implemented and gives the identical best value 0.228909 on Hepatitis, so the A8 choice is not driving the match.
Level 2 branch uses S2 = (match_counts >= 1) & (idx != i), i.e. the union over samples matching any observed feature (Eqs. 11-12); triggered for 106 entries.

Level 3 falls back to the global per-feature bin prior derived from bin frequencies (Eq. 13-14), but on Hepatitis the level-3 count is 0 at every nbins in {2,3,4,6,8}, so this code path is implemented yet never exercised by the run that produced the target.
proximity_kernel(Z, d) = (Z @ Z.T)/d (Eq. 15) is implemented and used for diagnostics (symmetry, min/max, diagonal); clustering itself is K-means on Z, consistent with the paper's protocol.
cluster.cluster_nmi uses sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=2 = ground-truth #classes, init='k-means++', n_init=10) and normalized_mutual_info_score (arithmetic) as the metric.
SEEDS = range(10); per-seed NMI lists of length 10 are stored in results/metrics.json and averaged.
NBINS_GRID = [2,3,4,6,8]; cluster.search_nbins evaluates the full grid and selects the per-dataset best mean NMI (nbins=2 selected). The whole search is logged in metrics.json/per_nbins.
